transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for having me. Um, am I okay to just start? Okay, great. 

Well, the main reason I’m here is... it’s actually a little embarrassing to admit, to be honest. I work as a health services manager, and I really do try to do a good job, but... I’ve noticed that whenever I have to do anything that takes real, you know, sitting-down brain work, I just... I struggle. 

Like, if I have to do the monthly reports or plan out a big multi-site health event, it feels like I just hit a wall. I end up putting it off and putting it off, even when I know it really matters and people are counting on me. I mean, I handle the day-to-day stuff just fine, I promise! But those big tasks... I hope that doesn't just sound like I'm being lazy. I really do care about my work. Does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing you usually see people for?
Do you feel anxious when you think about or start working on those big tasks?

Anxious? Um... no, I don't think so. I wouldn't really use the word anxious. I hope I'm answering that right, but I don't get, you know, a racing heart or feel panicked or anything like that. I actually handle workplace stress pretty well most of the time! 

It’s more just... I don't know, a really strong urge to do literally anything else? Like my brain just won't engage with the task. But I'm not sitting there terrified of the work, I promise. I really don't want you to think I can't handle my job or that I'm easily overwhelmed. I just sort of stare at the screen and feel stuck. Is that an okay way to describe it? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you find it hard to focus or pay attention to details in your daily work or other activities?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I really try to be careful, I promise. But... yeah, sometimes little things slip by me. 

Like, I'll be sending out the staffing schedule for the clinic, or even just an email for the kids' soccer league I help with, and I'll think I've looked it over perfectly. But then someone will reply and point out that I put the wrong date, or I completely forgot to list the location. It's so embarrassing when that happens. It's just little details that I know I should have caught, and I usually would have, but my brain just sort of skims right over them. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound incompetent. I do try my best to double-check things. Is that... is that normal for people to do sometimes?
Do you generally enjoy tasks that require a lot of mental effort when you're not at work?

Um, outside of work? Well, I try to keep things pretty light, to be honest. I mean, I don't really go out of my way to do things that take a ton of brainpower when I'm off the clock. 

I guess I just... I like to relax. So I don't really have a lot of hobbies that require intense concentration or anything. I hope that's okay to say. It's not that I couldn't do them if I tried, I just... I prefer to unwind, you know? Like watching TV or just hanging out. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm answering what you're actually asking.
Do you think you would be able to focus on those big tasks at work if you really wanted to?

Um... well, that's kind of the tricky part, and honestly, it's the main reason I decided to come in and talk to you. I really, really want to be able to focus on them. I know how important they are. 

But when it comes to that real, sitting-down brain work... like doing the monthly clinic reports or trying to plan out those big multi-site health events... it just feels like I hit a wall. I keep putting it off, even when I know it matters and I genuinely want to get it done. 

I really don't want it to seem like I'm just lazy or not trying hard enough, because I really do try. It's just... it's like my brain won't cooperate no matter how much I want it to. I hope that doesn't sound like a terrible excuse. Does that make sense, what I'm trying to say?
Have you always had trouble with focusing on tasks that require a lot of mental effort, or is this something that has developed over time?

Um... well, it hasn't always been like this, I don't think. I mean, I used to be able to manage everything okay, for the most part. 

It's really just been the last couple of years... maybe almost two years? About a year and eleven months, to be exact. I lost a really close friend around then, which was... well, it was hard. And after that happened, I ended up taking on a lot more of the responsibilities for the soccer league and some of the community outreach stuff we do, just to help out, you know? 

So I think maybe it's just that I have a lot on my plate right now, and that's why I'm struggling a bit more with the heavy mental lifting. I really hope it's just a temporary thing and not a sign that I'm slipping or anything. Does it sound like it could just be the extra stress from taking all that on? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture.
Do you often feel tired or drowsy during the day?

Um, tired during the day? Well, I mean, I wouldn't say I'm falling asleep at my desk or anything like that. I try to stay pretty active and keep moving, you know? 

I guess I have normal energy levels for the most part. I mean, everyone gets a little sluggish in the afternoon sometimes, right? But I wouldn't say I feel overly drowsy or anything that would be, like, a big problem. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I just don't want you to think I'm completely exhausted all the time, because I do try to keep my energy up. Is that okay?
Do you often feel sad or down when you're not able to complete those big tasks at work?

Um... well, no, I wouldn't really say I feel sad or down. I mean, I get a little frustrated with myself, sure, because I know I should be getting it done. But it's not like I'm sitting around crying about it or feeling depressed, you know? 

I really try to stay positive and just tell myself I'll do better the next day. I don't want to sound like I'm, you know, falling apart over it or anything. I just get annoyed that I'm dragging my feet. That's a pretty normal reaction, right? I just want to make sure I'm not making it sound worse than it is.
Do you have trouble focusing or putting in mental effort when doing things you enjoy, like hobbies or activities outside of work?

Um... no, not really. I mean, when it's something I actually want to do, like, you know, the soccer league stuff or working on a project in the garage, I'm usually fine. I can get into it and just go. 

It's really only the... the heavy paperwork or the really tedious reports at work that trip me up. If I'm doing something I enjoy, I don't really have that same mental block, I guess you could call it. I mean, everyone has an easier time doing things they like, right? That makes sense, doesn't it? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right idea—that I'm not totally incapable of focusing on anything at all.
Do you find it as hard to focus on tasks that you enjoy, as you do on the big tasks at work?

Um, no, definitely not. Like I was just saying, it's... it's a lot easier for me to focus when it's something I'm actually interested in. 

The stuff at work, the big tasks, that's where I really struggle to get started. But with my hobbies or things I enjoy, I don't have that problem at all. I can stay on track just fine. I think that's pretty normal, though, isn't it? I mean, nobody wants to do the boring stuff. I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right, that it's really just those big work projects that are the issue, not everything in my life. Is that helpful?
Do you have difficulty sustaining focus during conversations or when listening to others, such as in meetings or when someone is explaining something to you?

Um... well, sometimes, I guess. I mean, I wouldn't say I completely check out or anything rude like that. But, you know, if I'm in a meeting at the clinic and someone's going over, like, a budget update or something really dry... my mind might wander just a tiny bit. 

Like, if someone's phone vibrates on the table, or I can hear people talking out in the hallway, or even if I just suddenly remember something I forgot to do for the soccer league... I might kind of lose track of what's being said for a minute or two. But I usually catch back up! It's not like I'm ignoring people on purpose. I think everyone gets a little distracted in long meetings, right? I just want to make sure I don't sound like a terrible manager who doesn't listen to his team. That's just a normal thing that happens when there's a lot going on, isn't it?
Do you have trouble focusing when you're at home or in other settings outside of work?

Um... no, not really. I mean, at home, things are pretty relaxed, you know? It's not like the clinic where there's a million things pulling at me all at once. 

If I'm at home, I'm usually just hanging out, maybe watching a game or doing stuff around the house. I don't really have those big, stressful tasks hanging over my head like I do at work. So, no, I wouldn't say I have trouble focusing there. It's really just the heavy work stuff that gets me. That makes sense, right? Like, home is supposed to be where you can just kind of... chill out. I think most people are able to focus better when they're relaxed in their own space, don't you think?
Do you have trouble focusing when you're doing tasks that require a lot of mental effort with the soccer league or other activities outside of your health services manager job?

Um, no, not really with the soccer league. I mean, I guess there's some mental effort when I'm putting together the schedules or organizing the equipment orders, but... it's different, you know? It's soccer. I love it. 

So even if it takes some brainpower, I don't really find myself struggling to focus on it like I do with the big reports at the clinic. It feels more like fun than actual work, so I can usually just sit down and knock it out. I mean, I might take a break here and there, but I get it done without too much trouble. That's pretty typical, right? Like, if you're passionate about something, the mental effort doesn't feel as heavy. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture here... it's really just the big, stressful work stuff that throws me off. Does that sound okay to you?
Do you find that your difficulty with focusing on tasks is worse at certain times of the day?

Um... no, I haven't really noticed it being tied to a specific time of day. I mean, I guess if I'm tired at the end of the week, maybe I'm a little less sharp, but I think that happens to everyone, right? 

It's not like I wake up and can't focus, or hit a wall at exactly 2:00 PM every day. It's really just... if the task itself is overwhelming, like those big budget spreadsheets, that's when I struggle, whether it's morning or afternoon. If I'm doing something manageable, I'm usually fine. I try really hard to stay on top of things, so I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just spacing out all day long. That makes sense, doesn't it? That it's more about the task than the time on the clock?
Do you think you might be putting off those big tasks at work because they make you feel uncomfortable or stressed in some way, even if you don't feel anxious?

Um... well, maybe? I don't know if I'd call it stressed exactly, but... I guess I should just be honest. The main reason I’m actually here talking to you today is that anything that takes real, you know, sitting-down brain work... it just feels like I hit a wall. 

Like, if I have to do the monthly reports for the clinic, or if I'm supposed to be planning a big multi-site health event, I just keep putting it off. Even when I know it really matters and people are counting on me. I feel a little embarrassed admitting that, because I really don't want you to think I'm lazy or anything. I work hard and I care about my job a lot. It's just those heavy mental tasks that really trip me up. I'm sure a lot of people procrastinate on the big, tedious stuff though, right? That's a pretty normal reaction when something is just a lot to sit through, don't you think?
Do you think you would be able to focus on the big tasks at work if they were more interesting to you?

Um... I'm not really sure, to be honest. I guess maybe? But I really do try to find my work interesting, because I care a lot about the clinic and our staff. I don't want it to sound like I'm the kind of person who only wants to do the fun stuff and ignores the rest, you know? I know it's my job as a manager to handle the dry, boring things too. 

So... I don't know if making them more interesting would magically fix it. Even when I know a report is super important and I really, truly want to do a good job on it, I still just kind of get stuck. I hope that doesn't make me sound unprofessional. It's just hard to say for sure if interest is the missing piece there. Does that make sense?
Do you think your lack of focus on big tasks at work is because you're not motivated to do them?

Um... no, I really don't think it's a lack of motivation. I mean, I'm actually very motivated to do my job well. I really value my role at the clinic, and I want to be someone my team can rely on. I'd hate for anyone to think I just don't care or that I'm slacking off. 

It's more like... I have the motivation, I sit down with the intention of getting it done, but my brain just sort of... won't cooperate with the plan. It's frustrating because I *want* to do it. I really do. I hope you can see that I'm trying my best, and it's not just me being lazy or unmotivated. That's a big distinction, isn't it? Because I really do care about my work.
Do you think you've always had some difficulty with focusing, even as a child?

Um... well, I guess if I really think back on it... maybe a little bit? I mean, I was a good kid, I wasn't disruptive or anything like that. I really liked school. But... well, I suppose my teachers did used to tell my parents that I was, um, daydreaming a lot. 

They always said I was bright, which was nice of them, but... yeah, I guess I had a habit of losing worksheets or, you know, forgetting to turn in my homework. My mom actually had to check my backpack every single night just to make sure things got handed in. I feel a little silly admitting that I needed that much help back then, but I guess a lot of kids are a little scatterbrained in elementary school, right? It doesn't necessarily mean there was something wrong with me, does it? I just... I had my head in the clouds sometimes, I suppose.
Have you ever been diagnosed with or considered having ADHD?

Um... no, no, I haven't. I mean, I've never been diagnosed with it, and I... I don't think I've really considered it before, to be honest. 

I guess when I think of ADHD, I think of... well, little boys who are bouncing off the walls and can't sit still in class. And that was never me, you know? I was quiet. I wasn't causing trouble. So it just never crossed my mind, or my parents' minds, I suppose. 

I hope it doesn't seem like I'm wasting your time by being here if it turns out to be nothing. I just... I want to figure out why I'm struggling so much lately. Is it... do you think it's possible for someone like me, at my age, to have something like that? Even if I'm not hyperactive?
Do you often find yourself making careless mistakes or overlooking details in your work or other activities?

Um... well, I guess... occasionally? I mean, I try really, really hard to be thorough. I don't want you to think I'm just rushing through things without caring. I always try to double-check my work. 

But... yeah, I suppose lately, I have had a few little slip-ups. Like, I'll send out the staffing schedule for the clinic, or maybe an email for the kids' soccer league I help manage, and I'll be so sure I got it all right. And then... someone will reply and point out that I put down the wrong date, or I completely left off the location for a game. 

It's embarrassing, honestly. I usually catch things like that. It's just these silly little details that seem to slip past me, even when I feel like I'm paying attention. I hope that doesn't make me sound incompetent. I really do try to be careful. Is that... is that the kind of thing you mean?
